clue.text: Obscure setting for a Greek tormented by nightmares

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the first word here surrounds the piece that follows

parts.note: to obscure something is to keep it hidden

explanation.surface: Some unclear backdrop for a Greek figure who suffers bad dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ridden by a hag in folklore is plagued by nightmares, so the phrase means tormented or harassed.

clue.text: Musical functions for Mohicans

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
dos are parties or social functions

explanation.surface: Show tunes performed at gatherings for Native American tribespeople.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a punk hairstyle with a central crest, so Mohicans are examples of styled haircuts.

clue.text: Leaders of government overseeing an Indian state

indicators.note: the leaders of a set of words are their opening letters, taken from each in turn

explanation.surface: Top officials of a national government supervising one of India's regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small coastal state on India's west coast, a former Portuguese colony.

clue.text: Work reciprocally writing popular treatise about drug

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the treatise word encloses the drug

parts.note: a tract is a short treatise
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An author writes a bestselling essay on narcotics, working in partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on one another is to work reciprocally, each party influencing the other.

clue.text: Spirit identified in temperance movement's publicity?

parts.note: dry describes those opposed to alcohol, as in the temperance movement
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A ghost or spirit spotted in the anti-alcohol campaign's posters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph of Greek myth, a nature spirit.

clue.text: Gold coins once encapsulating Northumberland's magnanimity

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the coins wrap around the county piece

parts.note: nobles were gold coins minted in medieval England
Northumberland lies in the North East, NE, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Old gold money held in a northern county shows its generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobleness of spirit is greatness of mind and generosity, the same quality as magnanimity.

clue.text: Drive train regularly away from hazard

indicators.note: away from means these letters are taken out of the hazard word

parts.note: to imperil is to hazard or endanger

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word train is picked

explanation.surface: A locomotive drives on its schedule, steering clear of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of train, R and I, which leave IMPERIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push forward, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bad reputation of girl with trendy following

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl gains notoriety along with her fashionable fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is notoriety, being widely known for something bad.

clue.text: Exasperating expert introducing case

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
the vocative is a grammatical case used in addressing someone

explanation.surface: A specialist presenting a legal case in an irritating way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provocative deliberately provokes or annoys, so it is exasperating.

clue.text: Cement mix covering openwork in fortification

indicators.note: covering means the cement word goes around the openwork word

parts.note: lute is a clay or cement mixture used to seal joints
net is a fabric of open mesh, an openwork

explanation.surface: Builders mix mortar to cover lattice work in a castle wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a crescent-shaped outwork or detached bastion in military fortification.

clue.text: Unsuitably enters game in country, lacking ace

indicators.note: enters means the game word goes inside the shortened country
lacking means the ace letter is removed from the country

parts.note: Italy is a country
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
nap is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone joins a game abroad clumsily, without their best card.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something inaptly is doing it in an inappropriate or unsuitable way.

clue.text: Jester in birthday suit, wearing nothing

parts.note: in the buff means naked, wearing only one's birthday suit
O looks like zero, nothing
if you have a hat on, you are wearing it

explanation.surface: A court jester performing stark naked with no clothes at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a clown or joker, someone who plays the fool like a jester.

clue.text: It's almost prissy to raise scruples

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: demure can mean primly or affectedly modest, prissy

explanation.surface: A fussy person feels it is nearly prudish to voice objections.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to object or hesitate, voicing scruples about something.

clue.text: City pub tipsy Poles aim to go round

indicators.note: to go round means the shuffled letters surround the pub word
tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Drunk Polish drinkers plan to buy another round in a city bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' tells you to shuffle the Poles and aim; 'to go round' wraps that jumble about the pub word. The surface's round of drinks is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Minneapolis is the largest city in Minnesota in the United States.

clue.text: Dish consisting of bad meat or stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook in a mix, so the letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A dish made of spoiled beef or a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for an attractive person, and a dreamboat is exactly that.

clue.text: Series of compositions that transported Daisy?

definitions.meaning: a set of musical pieces meant to be performed together
the old song Daisy Bell has her on a bicycle made for two, the cycle of a song

explanation.surface: A suite of music that once carried a girl named Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song Daisy Bell ends with the line 'a bicycle made for two', hence a cycle from a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A song cycle is a group of songs written to be performed in sequence.

clue.text: Noble setting for head of lost legion

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the noble word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a countess is a noblewoman

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's mount for the leader of a lost army legion.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as an adjective means very numerous, as in 'their fans are legion', so countless.

clue.text: Lie around listening to 14, perhaps

indicators.note: listening to means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: lays are songs, like those in a song cycle

explanation.surface: Lounging about while listening to music.
explanation.definitionFit: To laze is to idle or lie about doing nothing.

clue.text: An utterer of notes? Judges sometimes assumed it

definitions.meaning: a songbird, the warbler that sings
the black square of cloth judges once donned to pass a death sentence

explanation.surface: Something spoken by a forger, and worn by judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The blackcap is a warbler; the judge's black cap was worn when sentencing to death.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackcap is a singing warbler, and also the cap judges wore for death sentences.

clue.text: Elder, possibly, that trod the boards

definitions.meaning: the elder is one example of a plant of this kind
Herbert Beerbohm ... was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: An older person who once acted on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub or small woody plant; Herbert Beerbohm Tree was an actor.

clue.text: They may be thick, but they have taking ways

definitions.meaning: from the idiom 'as thick as ...', meaning very close friends
they take things belonging to others

explanation.surface: Some people are stupid but charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbers take what is not theirs and are proverbially thick, close-knit.

clue.text: Peacekeepers retail sound food, showing concern for others

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces

indicators.note: sound means the words are judged by how they are heard

parts.note: to retail is to sell
fish is a food

explanation.surface: Soldiers sell healthy food in a caring spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' means the word for retail is heard, not spelt, and its double L is lost before the food word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being altruistic means caring about others' needs rather than one's own.

clue.text: Shamefaced swine restraining a no-good daughter

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the swine word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a hog is a pig, a swine
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A pig holds back a worthless daughter, looking guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is one of shame or guilt.

clue.text: Like the unfocused vision of tragic king in past

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: by can mean past, as in walking by
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: Lear's blurred eyesight in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim and blurred, unable to see sharply.

clue.text: Unwise, breaking limit — cop follows one

indicators.note: follows means the anagram comes after the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: breaking signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking the speed limit with a policeman behind is unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' says the speed limit and the cop are jumbled together; 'follows' puts the jumble after the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolitic means injudicious or unwise in a social or political sense.

clue.text: Confronted with this, puny Scots couldn't give a toss!

definitions.text: Confronted with this, puny Scots couldn't give a toss!

parts.words: Confronted with this, puny Scots couldn't give a toss!
parts.note: the idiom 'couldn't give a toss' means not caring; here it literally means unable to throw the heavy pole of Highland games

explanation.surface: Weak Scotsmen don't care about the challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The caber toss is a Highland games event of hurling a heavy tree trunk.

clue.text: Completely comfortable at last in social group

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the group

parts.note: a clan is a family or social group

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word comfortable

explanation.surface: Feeling finally at ease within a community.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean as an adverb means utterly or totally, as in 'clean forgot'.

clue.text: Very bad time for a small community

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Hard times for a little town.
explanation.definitionFit: A village is a small settlement in the countryside.

clue.text: Make much noise outside clubs, being dim

indicators.note: outside means the noise phrase surrounds the clubs letter

parts.note: to be loud is to make much noise
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: Being noisy outside a nightclub, being dim.
explanation.definitionFit: To becloud is to obscure or make dim and unclear.

clue.text: Form of witchcraft no good in desert

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter is dropped from the desert

parts.note: the Gobi is a desert in Asia

explanation.surface: Witchcraft is useless in the wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, or obeah, is a form of Caribbean folk magic.

clue.text: Impertinent American soldier's first year with specialist troops

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, the British army's special forces regiment

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word soldier's

explanation.surface: A rude Yank soldier begins a year with elite troops.
explanation.walkthrough: SAS is the British Special Air Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy is a mainly American word for cheeky or impudent.

clue.text: Lose footing taking drink outside for youngster

indicators.note: outside means the drink goes around the stumble

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail, such as the Singapore sling
to trip is to lose your footing

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles holding a drink for a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a young man, a youth.
